bruce-peak.name: Bruce Peak
bruce-peak.fact: The highest point on Saltspring Island.

specialties.text: The highest mountain in all the Gulf Islands
Look for the radio and phone towers on top

mount-tuam.name: Mount Tuam
mount-tuam.fact: A steep mountain at the south end of Saltspring Island.

specialties.text: Its steep southeast slope is a nature reserve

mount-maxwell.name: Mount Maxwell
mount-maxwell.fact: Its cliff-top park has one of the best views in the Gulf Islands.

specialties.text: Made a park in 1938 for its amazing views
A great spot to watch the sunset over Burgoyne Bay

mount-galiano.name: Mount Galiano
mount-galiano.fact: Hikers climb it to watch the ferries go through Active Pass.

specialties.text: On clear days you can see Mount Baker from the top

mount-parke.name: Mount Parke
mount-parke.fact: The highest point on Mayne Island.

specialties.text: Its ridge trail gives wide views of land and sea
Look for ravens, eagles and turkey vultures

mount-norman.name: Mount Norman
mount-norman.fact: The highest point of the Pender Islands, in Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.

specialties.text: A wooden lookout deck sits at the very top
Named in 1860 after a Royal Navy paymaster

mount-warburton-pike.name: Mount Warburton Pike
mount-warburton-pike.fact: Saturna Island's highest point, looking over Boundary Pass to the USA.

specialties.text: Named for Warburton Pike, an explorer and author
Wild goats roam its long, rocky ridge

mount-newton.name: Mount Newton
mount-newton.fact: A forested hill on the Saanich Peninsula, south of the Swartz Bay terminal.

knowledge.tagline: A forest park on the peninsula

specialties.text: Its park was BC's first donated park, in 1921

grouse-mountain.name: Grouse Mountain
grouse-mountain.fact: A ski hill above North Vancouver. Its lights twinkle at night.

specialties.text: Hikers climb the Grouse Grind: about 2,800 steps!
A big cable car carries people to the top

mount-seymour.name: Mount Seymour
mount-seymour.fact: A ski mountain in Mount Seymour Provincial Park, North Vancouver.

specialties.text: A provincial park since 1936
Skiing, snowshoeing and sledding in winter

black-mountain.name: Black Mountain
black-mountain.fact: Part of Cypress Provincial Park, above West Vancouver.

specialties.text: Its ski area, Cypress, hosted 2010 Olympic events

mount-constitution.name: Mount Constitution
mount-constitution.fact: The highest point of the San Juan Islands, in the USA. A stone tower stands on top.

knowledge.tagline: Top of the San Juan Islands

specialties.text: Its stone tower was finished in 1936
It stands in Moran State Park, on Orcas Island

saltspring-island.name: Saltspring Island
saltspring-island.fact: The biggest and busiest of the Southern Gulf Islands.

specialties.text: A big Saturday market in Ganges, spring to fall
Its fall fair has run since the 1890s
Black pioneers from California settled here in 1859
Named for the salty springs at its north end

galiano-island.name: Galiano Island
galiano-island.fact: A long, skinny island. Its south tip lines Active Pass.

specialties.text: Named after a Spanish explorer who came in 1792
Bluffs Park looks down on ferries in Active Pass
Montague Harbour has bright white shell beaches
Waves have carved caves into its sandstone shore

north-pender-island.name: North Pender Island
north-pender-island.fact: A little bridge joins it to South Pender Island.

specialties.text: A canal split it from South Pender in 1903
A big disc golf course winds through its forest
The island's fall fair is held each August
A Saturday farmers' market at the Community Hall

south-pender-island.name: South Pender Island
south-pender-island.fact: The quieter Pender, joined to North Pender by a little bridge.

specialties.text: A one-lane bridge joined the Penders in 1955
Boats from the USA have checked in here since 1958
Trails climb Mount Norman in the national park

mayne-island.name: Mayne Island
mayne-island.fact: Gold miners rested at its Miners Bay on the way to the Fraser River gold rush.

specialties.text: A lighthouse has guarded Active Pass since 1885
Its tiny museum is the island's old 1896 jail
A Japanese garden honours families sent away in 1942
Its August fall fair began in the 1920s

saturna-island.name: Saturna Island
saturna-island.fact: A remote, hard-to-reach island. Much of it is national park.

specialties.text: A Canada Day lamb barbecue, held since 1950
East Point is a top spot to watch orcas from land
East Point's lighthouse first shone in 1888

prevost-island.name: Prevost Island
prevost-island.fact: A quiet island with no ferry, between Saltspring and Mayne.

specialties.text: One family has farmed most of it since the 1920s
Parts of its shore are in the national park
Named after the captain of HMS Satellite

moresby-island.name: Moresby Island
moresby-island.fact: A small island at the south end of Swanson Channel.

specialties.text: A private cattle farm, closed to visitors
Named after Royal Navy admiral Fairfax Moresby

portland-island.name: Portland Island
portland-island.fact: Part of Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. You can only get there by boat.

specialties.text: BC gave it to Princess Margaret in 1958
She gave it back in 1967, and it became a park
A ship sunk here in 1991 is now a reef for fish

piers-island.name: Piers Island
piers-island.fact: A small island right next to the Swartz Bay terminal.

specialties.text: A 1930s prison held Doukhobor protesters here

sidney-island.name: Sidney Island
sidney-island.fact: It has a long sandy spit, part of a national park.

specialties.text: Its long, sandy spit is part of the national park
A factory made bricks from its clay, 1906 to 1915
Its lagoon is protected as a home for birds

james-island.name: James Island
james-island.fact: Long ago it had a factory that made explosives.

specialties.text: Its factory made TNT in both World Wars
Hundreds of workers once lived in a village here
Today it's private, with a golf course

saanich-peninsula.name: Saanich Peninsula
saanich-peninsula.fact: A peninsula of Vancouver Island, north of Victoria. The Swartz Bay terminal is at its north end.

specialties.text: The Saanich Fair: Labour Day weekend, since 1868
Butchart Gardens bloom in an old stone quarry
Its 1918 telescope was briefly the world's largest

swartz-bay-terminal.name: Swartz Bay terminal
swartz-bay-terminal.fact: Where this ferry docks on Vancouver Island.

tsawwassen-terminal.name: Tsawwassen terminal
tsawwassen-terminal.fact: Where this ferry docks on the mainland, at the end of a long causeway.

tsawwassen.name: Tsawwassen
tsawwassen.fact: A mainland community, home of the Tsawwassen First Nation.

specialties.text: Huge flocks of shorebirds stop at Boundary Bay
Boundary Bay's shallow water gets warm in summer

roberts-bank.name: Roberts Bank
roberts-bank.fact: A huge port where coal trains unload and container ships dock.

sidney.name: Sidney
sidney.fact: A seaside town near the Swartz Bay terminal.

specialties.text: Known as a book town, with several bookshops
A seaside aquarium shows Salish Sea creatures
A Thursday-night street market runs all summer

point-roberts.name: Point Roberts (USA)
point-roberts.fact: Part of the USA, but you can only drive there through Canada!

knowledge.tagline: A little piece of the USA

specialties.text: One of the best places to see orcas from land

vancouver.name: Vancouver
vancouver.fact: The heart of Canada's third-biggest metro area.

active-pass.name: Active Pass
active-pass.fact: A narrow, twisty pass. Strong tides rush through and ferries turn sharply.

swanson-channel.name: Swanson Channel
swanson-channel.fact: The channel between Saltspring and North Pender. Orcas sometimes travel through it.

satellite-channel.name: Satellite Channel
satellite-channel.fact: Named after HMS Satellite, a navy ship from the 1850s.

haro-strait.name: Haro Strait
haro-strait.fact: The Canada–USA border runs down this strait.

boundary-pass.name: Boundary Pass
boundary-pass.fact: The Canada–USA border runs through this pass.

strait-of-georgia.name: Strait of Georgia
strait-of-georgia.fact: Part of the Salish Sea, between Vancouver Island and the mainland.
